flashcard_questions.q: Which work is the Badinerie the final movement of?
flashcard_questions.a: Orchestral Suite No. 2 in B minor.

flashcard_questions.q: In which years was that orchestral suite composed?
What does the word badinerie mean?
Which solo instrument carries the melody in the Badinerie?
Which keyboard instrument plays the basso continuo in the Badinerie?

flashcard_questions.a: A partly improvised accompaniment played above a bass line.

flashcard_questions.q: Which form is the Badinerie written in?
In which key does the Badinerie begin?
In which key does Section A of the Badinerie end?
What is motif X in the Badinerie?
flashcard_questions.a: A descending B minor arpeggio with a quaver-and-semiquaver rhythm.

flashcard_questions.q: What is motif Y in the Badinerie?
flashcard_questions.a: An ascending semiquaver figure of broken chords and stepwise movement.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the time signature of the Badinerie?
In which bar does a Neapolitan sixth chord appear?
How wide is the flute's pitch range in the Badinerie?

notes: 15 cards: 4 background cards (composer, parent suite, composition years, meaning of the title), 3 instrumentation cards, 3 structure and key cards taken exactly as the content states them, 2 motif-identification cards (X descending, Y ascending), plus time signature, the bar-35 Neapolitan sixth and the two-octave flute range. Dropped the long trill and suspension bar lists, which would only produce enumeration answers, and dropped terraced dynamics because the dynamics lesson already tests it.
